submission.justification: Sensor-T3 gives the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um at 150 um in the 2025 summary), but after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency is only 82.0% with strong charge trapping and no full depletion, far below the >=97% end-of-life requirement, so it is excluded. Sensor-T2 meets the radiation requirement (99.2%) but its resolution is about 13.7-14.6 um across 100-200 um. Sensor-T1 meets the requirement (98.5% after irradiation) and gives the best resolution among the viable options. Its simulated resolution is 9.3 um at 100 um, 8.80 um at 125 um, 8.86 um at 150 um, 9.14 um at 160 um, 9.17 um at 200 um. The 125-150 um range is the minimum, and differences of roughly 0.1-0.3 um are within the simulation scatter. I chose 125 um, the lowest measured point, which also means less charge trapping to lose after irradiation. Caveat: resolution was simulated only unirradiated; the end-of-life resolution of T1 was not simulated, and the 98.5% efficiency comes from a separate test-beam campaign.
